parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime imposes universal, traveller-facing exposures: national passports must show sex assigned at birth, a foreign-ministry cable directs officers to refuse and investigate document/sex discrepancies with potential lifetime fraud findings, and the state/province mandates birth-certificate facilities at every school and college. Detention in national custody (forced labour, abuse of trans detainees) is documented. No criminal exposure attaches to this state/province's own facility law (no enforcement mechanism, no arrests sourced), the care ban is re-enjoined, and municipal protections and national hate-crime law partially operate. This is tier-1/2 universal exposure without working remedy, but short of criminalised targeting or custody-by-default: materially above the 0.25 tier, around the 0.45–0.55 band.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport markers restricted to birth sex; officers instructed to refuse and investigate discrepancies; suspected 'misrepresentation of sex' can support permanent fraud ineligibility. Trans travellers report confiscation and stranding; allied governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic; limited waiver possible; X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; policy is under active court challenge.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch can flow into investigation, visa refusal, or fraud adjudication at the national level regardless of state/province protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau mandates haircutting, hormone withdrawal and 'psychiatric' substitution for trans inmates; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or visa overstay routes the visitor into this national custody regime; consular/litigation recourse only partial.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law mandates birth-certificate facilities at all K-12 schools and public/private colleges; national facility bans cover government buildings in many states; no congruent-facility right in government buildings here.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state's facility statute has no enforcement mechanism and no criminal penalty; no arrests or citations documented under it; single-occupancy restrooms exempt.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facility orders and state designation rules combine; in other states bathroom trespass is criminalised, but not documented here.

care_services.exposure: Under-18 care banned by statute whose enforcement status is unresolved (re-enjoined, under appeal); hospital-records subpoenas and funding threats chill care provision.
care_services.protection: Adult care remains lawful; the state appeals court re-enjoined the minor-care ban; January 2024 intrusive adult-care rules were withdrawn.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's care access depends on the litigation state at travel time; national proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for minors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive rhetoric ('chemical and surgical mutilation', 'radical gender ideology'), counterterrorism strategy listing 'radically pro-transgender' groups, criminal referral of teachers facilitating minor transitions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; strategy states disagreement is not targeted; hate-crime statute covers gender identity nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing raises outing probability and police/hostility climate; enforcement is contested and uneven.

minors_guardians.exposure: Schools must out students to parents (Jan 2025 law); facility and sports restrictions target minors; care ban partially operative.
minors_guardians.protection: Care ban re-enjoined; sports enforcement likewise uncertain; opt-outs exist for curriculum.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling parent risks a minor being outed by school staff or barred from congruent facilities or care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Bias incidents documented; 37 states lacked gender-identity bias statutes (2019); one documented restroom arrest in another state; this state's tier is second-highest of five.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment discrimination barred nationally and in state employment; 33 municipal ordinances cover public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse depends on locality; state private-accommodation discrimination is unprotected.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No private-sector gender-identity discrimination statute at state level; county refusal of birth-certificate corrections; no remedy for designation itself.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on documents; active litigation may restore passport policy; municipal ordinances and courts provide partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are fragmented, slow, and cannot reach the national document regime while litigation is pending.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable universal exposure: every trans visitor passes through document/sex verification with durable records, plus threat-framing by the state. Here severity is higher (fraud ineligibility, abusive custody) but custody and prosecution are not typical outcomes, and municipal protections partially operate — similar tier, slightly harsher tail.

Like 0.55-B, exposure centres on secondary scrutiny and administrative denial rather than criminalisation: refused cases, facility refusals, humiliations without arrest. This jurisdiction exceeds it through national custody abuse and fraud-findings, pulling below 0.55.

Not as severe: 0.25-C features criminalised facility entry with arrests and birth-sex prison placement with documented assault. Here the state facility law has no enforcement mechanism, the care ban is enjoined, and hate-crime and municipal protections operate — a clear step above 0.25.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor has trained border officers, functioning tribunals and compensation for unlawful detention. Here the national document regime and cable-based fraud exposure are the operative rule, with remedies stalled in litigation and no documented national-custody protection.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one combined regime: a national document and screening system that forces birth-sex disclosure, subjects discrepancies to investigation and possible lifetime fraud findings, and runs custody institutions that have abused trans detainees; a state layer that mandates incongruent facilities at schools and colleges with no local penalty, uncertain minor-care restrictions, and no private-discrimination statute; and patchy protections (national hate-crime law, employment coverage, municipal ordinances, active litigation) that do not reach the exposures a visitor actually faces. Worst operative feature is universal-exposure document/facility screening without working remedy, mitigated by the absence of local criminalisation and enjoined care bans — placing the jurisdiction in the middle of the Elevated Risk band.
